title: Prior Authorization Appeal Filing Windows and Decision Clocks — Prescription Insurance on File Plan Classes
content:
When a plan under **Prescription Insurance on File** denies a prior authorization, the plan class sets how long the patient has to appeal and the clocks on which the plan decides an appeal.

| Plan class | Appeal filing window (calendar days from the denial) | Standard appeal decision (calendar days) | Expedited appeal decision (hours) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Medicaid Managed Care Pharmacy Benefit | 60 | 30 | 72 |
| Medicare Part D Standard Plan | 65 | 7 | 72 |
| Medicare Part D Enhanced Plan | 65 | 7 | 72 |
| Medicare Advantage Prescription Drug Plan | 65 | 7 | 72 |
| Commercial High-Deductible Health Plan | 180 | 30 | 72 |
| Commercial Copay Plan | 180 | 30 | 72 |
| Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit | 30 | 30 | 72 |

## Definitions

- **Appeal filing window** — calendar days from a prior authorization denial within which an appeal may be filed.
- **Standard appeal decision** — calendar days the plan has to decide a standard appeal.
- **Expedited appeal decision** — hours the plan has to decide an expedited appeal.

## Reading across the classes

- The three Medicare classes decide a standard appeal in 7 calendar days; every other class takes 30.
- Every class decides an expedited appeal within 72 hours.
- The filing window is longest under the two commercial classes (180 days) and shortest under the Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit (30 days).
